Senses.Explanation: To look around is to turn and look at a person, direction, or assembly. The verb retains that visual sense in Emperor Suzong's complaint that Nanyang Huizhong does not look at him and in an unnamed monk's looking east and west for the absent Changqing Da'an. Chan records also make it a recurrent teaching-seat stage direction. At an opening of the hall Xuedou Chongxian “looked around at the assembly” (顧視大眾) before speaking; Yungai Zhiyong follows the look with a shout and questions concerning host and guest. In one encounter Mazu Daoyi merely looks, Yangshan Huiji comments on the look, and the exchange ends. Ciji Cong compresses speech and action still further: “then he looked around at the assembly and said, ‘stop!’” (乃顧視大眾曰休). Yulin Tongxiu looks left and right, strikes the staff, and leaves the seat (顧視左右，卓拄杖，下座). Thus an ordinary look is bent into an observable public-address action of the teaching seat; the entry does not assign the look an unspoken symbolic message.
Senses.Note: The stated direction or object is translated in context: “the assembly” (大眾), “left and right” (左右), or “east and west” (東西).

Occurrences.Kwic: 帝又問。師都不視之。曰。朕是大唐天子。師何以殊不顧視。師曰。還見虗空麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Nanyang Huizhong section. Emperor Suzong is the exact speaker who complains that Nanyang Huizhong does not look at him; Nanyang answers by asking whether empty space blinks at the emperor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 開堂日，於法座前顧視大眾，乃云：若論本分相見，不必高陞法座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄), Xuedou Chongxian section. Xuedou Chongxian is the exact actor who looks over the assembly before speaking at the opening of the hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師顧視大眾，喝一喝，云：諸禪德！莫是賓主歷然麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄), Yungai Zhiyong section. Yungai Zhiyong is the exact actor who looks over the assembly, shouts, and asks whether host and guest are distinct.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師乃顧視。仰曰。若恁麼。與哭何異。師便休。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Mazu Daoyi section. Mazu Daoyi is the exact actor who looks; Yangshan Huiji comments that such a response is no different from crying, and Mazu stops.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有僧上法堂。顧視東西。不見師。乃曰。好箇法堂。祇是無人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Changqing Da'an section. An unnamed monk is the exact actor who enters the hall, looks east and west for the absent master, and comments that the hall has no one in it. The six-rung ladder does not name him.
The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Ciji Cong section. Ciji Cong is the exact actor who looks around at the assembly and says, 'stop.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 顧視眾曰：夫為宗匠，隨處提綱。應機問答，殺活臨時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Xiangji Yongmin section. Xiangji Yongmin is the exact actor who looks over the assembly and then defines the responsive public work of a lineage teacher.
The Recorded Sayings of State Preceptor Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), in Yulin Tongxiu's own hall address. Yulin Tongxiu is the exact actor who looks left and right, strikes the staff, and leaves the seat.
